description: pkix-path/src/lib.rs:2105-2120 — In chain_walk's policy tree update loop, match_count is computed by calling tree.iter().filter(...).count() (one full scan of the tree), and then the code loops match_count times pushing PolicyNode values that are all structurally identical for a given p_oid (same depth, same valid_policy, same expected_policy_set). This is an O(2 * tree_size) scan per policy per certificate when the matched parents could be collected once and iterated. Additionally, collecting .count() and then pushing that many identical nodes effectively ignores which parent node matched — it's overcounting from an RFC 5280 perspective (at most one parent should match per valid_policy per depth in a well-formed tree). Use .filter(...).for_each(|_parent| new_nodes.push(...)) to scan once and make the parent available if its data is needed.
title: policy tree match_count scans tree twice per policy
